//: Seeing a blow coming (03 §7): an ordinary person of wits 10 takes a fifth of a second of their own time to notice a wind-up, one of wits 20 a tenth. Whoever notices in time may answer; whoever does not, cannot. Anyone directly controlled within 3 m is offered a blow aimed at someone else, for the reactions that may answer for another.

Whether a guard holds against a blow: how many times the one fighter is the other. A guard set in time is easier to keep than a blow is to force through it: each guard below weighs the attacker at half, so between equals a parry holds about nine times in ten.
name: Control

//: Whether a duck or a sway takes someone out of a blow's way.
name: Slip

//: Turning a blow with a blade held in the hand: the flat is set across the blow's line and most of it is turned aside. A parry holds what the parrier's strength can turn; much past that and the blade takes the rest, and what the blade cannot stop goes on to where the blow was aimed (07 §5.3, §14).
name: Parry

//: Taking a blow on a shield, or on the forearm where there is none: less is turned aside than by a parry, and what is not lands on the shield or the arm.
name: Block

//: Ducking or swaying out of a blow's line without leaving the spot: if it works, the blow misses (07 §5.2, slipping); if not, the one ducking is still harder to land on squarely (`evasion`, added to the aim's `against`).
name: Dodge

//: A quick step straight away from whoever opened the window: someone out of a blow's reach when it lands is simply missed, with no contest (07 §5.2, leaving). The step is taken as the spring ends, checked against the world as it then is.
name: Step back

//: A guard held up before anything comes: in force for as long as it is held, at the cost of an arm (07 §5.1). Letting go is a `Cancel`; it is not a foreground action, so its holder goes on deciding what to do.
name: Guard

//: How a watchman answers a blow he notices in time: a block, on a shield if he has one and on the forearm if not, else a duck (09 §6.3). A townsperson and a dog answer nothing.
The player is asked how to answer a blow they noticed in time, and time stops until they do (03 §7.3). A rule like any other: a mod may replace it, or a setting switch it off.
doc: Asks a directly controlled character how to answer a window it noticed. Off when the setting `core:ask_reactions` is false.

//: Stances that answer by themselves (07 §12): attach one to a character and it reacts to every blow it notices in time. The AI attaches or replaces these as a character's stance changes.
doc: Parries every blow its holder notices in time.
Blocks every blow its holder notices in time.
Ducks every blow its holder notices in time.
Steps back from every blow its holder notices in time.
